meta.name: Hive
meta.tagline: Tu colmena de agentes IA. Local-first. Multi-canal. Open source. Construido desde Colombia para el mundo.
meta.product_type: Agent Harness — per README's own positioning: pre-built operational infrastructure around an LLM (tools, memory, error handling, deployment, observability), explicitly NOT an agent framework (contrasted against LangChain/CrewAI/AutoGen in docs/HIVE-HARNESS.md). 'Runtime' in this document refers to packages/core specifically (the engine inside the harness), not a claim that Hive is 'just a runtime'.

external_integrations.storage_engine: @johpaz/hive-db v0.3.1 — embedded Rust engine: redb (KV) + tantivy (BM25 full-text) + hnsw_rs (vector search). Lives at ~/.hive/data/hivedb. Confirmed by source (zero bun:sqlite/better-sqlite3 usage left in packages/core/src) — note that README.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/HIVE-HARNESS.md still describe the store as SQLite (data/hive.db); those docs predate the HiveDB migration and are stale on this point.

runtime_flow.description: CLI (`hive start` / `hive dev`) launches the gateway: gateway/server.ts's startGateway().

Gateway boots HiveDB storage, ChannelManager, AgentService+AgentRunner, the durable queue + job executors, CronScheduler + DAGScheduler + task-driver, canvasManager, and the voice/multimodal services.
Gateway registers ~20 REST route modules and serves the pre-built hive-ui SPA.
Inbound channel messages, webchat turns, and cron/DAG triggers become jobs (chat_turn, goal_run, project_task, worker_task) on the durable queue.
job-executors run each job through agent-loop.ts's runAgent, which calls out to llm-client (now retried via resilience/retry.ts) → llm-providers/*, and to tools/* via tool-runtime.

run-store checkpoints/leases each run in HiveDB; job-store/durable-queue do the same for jobs, now with idempotency keys and logical-failure retry with backoff (separate from crash/lease-expiry recovery).
goal-runner + proof-packet + run-epoch verify acceptance criteria and record a ProofPacketDoc once per completed run, fixing the provider/model/tool-catalog epoch it was checked under.
Results are pushed back to the originating channel and/or streamed live to the hive-ui SPA over WebSocket.

current_release.name: Durable execution harness: retry, idempotency, epoch-fingerprinted proof packets
current_release.summary: Adds a generic retry-with-backoff utility and enhances run orchestration with acceptance criteria, epoch tracking, and configurable lease durations, following the 'tool legibility' harness-engineering practice (discover → select → invoke → interpret → verify) documented in docs/TOOL-CONVENTIONS.md.

changed_files.change: wraps callLLM in withRetry using config-driven policy, respects abort signal
adds acceptance criteria array to GoalRunOptions; verifyGoal verifies each criterion independently and conjuncts verdicts
acceptance_json/epoch_json fields on runs; lease durations now config-driven instead of hardcoded
adds failJobOrRetry path for logical-failure retry, periodic re-dispatch of delayed jobs, idempotency_key passthrough
largest diff: idempotency_key dedup, JobRetryPolicy/computeBackoffDelay, failJobOrRetry, retry_count/last_error fields
tags failures with retryable/isRetryableError; project_task/goal_run now call buildProofPacket on completion
passes harness config into initDurableQueue; /health reports queue depth, expired leases, active run count, boot id
exposes preferred_cron_channel in the cron-channels API
exposes preference field in the users API
new ProofPacketDoc; acceptance_json/epoch_json on AgentRunDoc; retry_count/last_error/idempotency_key on JobDoc
new indexes for idempotency_key and proofPackets lookups
scheduled/cron task runs now stream live tool/text narration to the user's channel
unrelated bundled fix: auto-links a Telegram chat to the single-user account on first contact
UI side of cron-channel-preference fix: reads useNotesAndCronsStore/cronChannels, keys options by channel id, reads server preference instead of hardcoding 'auto'

docs.summary: Defines 'tool legibility' conventions for tools/ and tool-runtime/, based on the harness-engineering discover→select→invoke→interpret→verify practice: (a) dry-run mode (dryRun?: boolean) for any tool with side effects, (b) bounded/stable output shapes (truncate, avoid data: any), (c) stable structured failure signatures ({code, message, hint}) so job-executors.ts can classify retryability via resilience/retry.ts#isRetryableError.
